observation.visible_scene: A night scene over a calm body of water. A low, distant city skyline with scattered lights sits on the horizon, and a dark landform/embankment cuts diagonally across the foreground left. Above the skyline a fireworks display is in progress: a row of white/gold radial starburst patterns spans the center of the sky, with greenish spherical burst clusters higher up, and all of these are mirrored as elongated shimmering reflections on the water. The camera is essentially fixed throughout.
visible_changes: At the start the upper green spherical clusters are still dense and bright; over roughly the first half second they spread out and fade until they are largely gone, while the lower white radial starbursts stay in place.
The white radial starburst patterns hold nearly constant position and shape across the whole excerpt, only slowly dimming, rather than expanding outward or drifting.
Small red/pink ember dots appear near the top of the sky around mid-excerpt and then fade again.
As the white bursts dim toward the end, the sky patterns and their water reflections become dominated by scattered colored (red/green/yellow) embers instead of bright white spokes.

The water reflections track the sky content: bright white streaks early, then more muted and multicolored streaks later; the skyline and foreground landform do not move, indicating no camera pan/zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: The launch and initial explosion of these bursts occurred before the first frame; this clip shows only the afterglow/dispersal phase.
Whether additional bursts ignite after the last frame is not shown.
The cause of the slight overall brightness changes (fade of embers vs. exposure) is not determinable from the frames.
uncertain_details: Exact hue of some fading embers (red vs. pink vs. orange) is hard to confirm in the dark.
Whether the apparent stability of the white starbursts is true stasis or very slow drift is uncertain at this frame rate.
Minor flicker in the reflections may be water motion or compression, not a new sky event.
